mainEntity.name: How much does a Honda Civic 1.6 i-DTEC engine replacement cost?

acceptedAnswer.text: A complete reconditioned Honda Civic 1.6 i-DTEC engine typically costs between £1,500 and £2,800 for supply only, while fully rebuilt units range from £2,500 to £4,000. Used engines are available from around £500.

mainEntity.name: What is the difference between the N16A4 and N16B5 Honda Civic 1.6 i-DTEC engines?

historyTimeline.h2: Honda Civic 1.6 i-DTEC - Engine History & Specs at a Glance
historyTimeline.intro: When the 1.6 i-DTEC variant launched, it served as the highly efficient, long-distance diesel workhorse of the Honda Civic range, introducing the Earth Dreams diesel architecture to replace the older 2.2 i-DTEC units with improved emissions and fuel economy.

milestones.description: N16A4 introduced, 1.6L i-DTEC, 120 PS (88 kW), replacing the 2.2 i-DTEC in the Mk9 Civic with a lighter block and improved fuel efficiency.
N16B5 introduced for the Mk10 Civic, maintaining the 120 PS output but featuring updated engine management, revised thermal management, and enhanced DPF integration for stricter Euro 6 compliance.

historyTimeline.closingNote: Every engine fitted to the Honda Civic 1.6 i-DTEC is covered below, with UK rebuilt pricing and known failure points.

commonProblems.h2: Honda Civic 1.6 i-DTEC Engine Problems - Repair Cost vs Replacement
commonProblems.h3: The Honda Civic 1.6 i-DTEC is a highly efficient and robust diesel, but modern emissions systems introduce specific failure points. The N16A4 and N16B5 codes dominate replacement demand for this variant. Rebuilt engines through EnginesMarket include upgraded components addressing these original failure points, plus a minimum 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty.

problems.h4: DPF Clogging & EGR Issues - Why the Honda Civic 1.6 i-DTEC (N16A4/N16B5) Suffers Premature Blockages
problems.rootCause: Frequent short, low-speed urban journeys prevent the Diesel Particulate Filter (DPF) from reaching the high temperatures required for active regeneration. Soot accumulates, increasing exhaust backpressure and forcing the EGR valve to stick, which can eventually lead to turbo strain or engine limp mode.

repairOptions.longevity: Temporary fix; blockage will return if driving habits do not change

problems.h4: Injector Failure - Why the Honda Civic 1.6 i-DTEC (N16A4/N16B5) Develops Rough Idling
problems.rootCause: Diesel injectors can suffer from internal wear or seal degradation over time, leading to fuel leak-off, rough idling, and difficulty starting. In severe cases, this can cause cylinder wash or excessive DPF soot loading.

items.question: What are the signs of DPF failure in a Honda Civic 1.6 i-DTEC?
items.answer: DPF failure in the Honda Civic 1.6 i-DTEC usually presents as a persistent engine management light, reduced power (limp mode), and poor fuel economy.
keyPoints: You may notice a strong smell of sulfur or diesel from the exhaust.
The vehicle may refuse to regenerate, leading to increased exhaust backpressure.
Ignoring these signs can lead to secondary turbocharger damage.

items.question: What is the difference between the N16A4 and N16B5 Honda Civic 1.6 i-DTEC engines?
